anchors.paper_title: Building Brain Invaders: EEG data of an experimental validation
anchors.paper_venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
anchors.reason: The candidate paper explicitly describes the dataset, mentioning it contains EEG recordings of 25 subjects testing the Brain Invaders P300, which matches the dataset's content.

metadata.methods_description: EEG data were recorded at 512 Hz sampling rate using 16 wet Silver/Silver Chloride electrodes in a standard 10-20 montage (Fp1, Fp2, F5, AFz, F6, T7, Cz, T8, P7, P3, Pz, P4, P8, O1, Oz, O2) with g.USBamp hardware and OpenVibe software. Reference electrode was placed at left earlobe with ground at FZ. Subjects performed visual P300 tasks with 36 symbols organized in 12 groups. Each session contained two runs (Non-Adaptive and Adaptive, randomized order), with training phases consisting of 80 target and 400 non-target flashes per run, and variable online phases based on performance. In Non-Adaptive mode, training data calibrated the MDM classifier for the online phase. In Adaptive mode, the classifier was initialized with generic class geometric means from a previous experiment and continuously adapted using Riemannian methods.

citation_details.title: P300 dataset BI2012 from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
citation_details.author: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 25 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task inspired by the Space Invaders video game. Participants viewed sequences of flashing alien groups and silently counted target stimuli while 16-channel EEG was recorded at 128 Hz. The dataset includes both training and online sessions with performance-dependent feedback, providing a benchmark resource for P300-based BCI research and algorithm development.

citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 24 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game paradigm. The study compares adaptive versus non-adaptive calibration approaches using Riemannian geometry for classifier training. EEG data were acquired using 16 electrodes at 512 Hz sampling rate during sessions conducted at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble, France in 2013.

citation_details.title: P300 dataset BI2012 from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
citation_details.author: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 25 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task inspired by the Space Invaders video game. Participants were presented with visual flashes of alien groups while 16-channel EEG was recorded at 128 Hz, with the objective of detecting target versus non-target stimuli. The dataset includes both training and online sessions with a total of 128 target trials and 640 non-target trials per subject, providing a benchmark resource for P300-based BCI research and algorithm development.
